title: Pioneer Prime status can be held once per chain and once per Prime Agent, permanently
content:
A.2.2.9.3.1.1 imposes a double uniqueness rule: "It is only possible for a Pioneer Chain to have a Pioneer Prime once, and for a Pioneer Prime to have the Pioneer Prime status with a single blockchain, once." A.2.2.9.3.1.2 makes Operational GovOps check both conditions — that the Prime Agent has not previously been a Pioneer Prime, and that the chain has not previously had one — before adding it to the list of Active Pioneer Primes.

Selection itself is delegated outward. A Prime Agent must "provide written proof to Operational GovOps that it has been provisionally designated as such by the official team or foundation of the relevant Pioneer Chain." Sky does not choose who pioneers a chain; the chain does, and Sky only verifies uniqueness. That outsources a judgment Sky is poorly placed to make — which Agent a target ecosystem will actually work with — to the party who knows.

The once-per-Prime limit is the more unusual half. It prevents a single well-capitalized Agent from accumulating Pioneer status across many chains and capturing the default-tagging benefit (A.2.2.9.3.1.3) ecosystem-wide. Pioneer rights are distributed across Agents by construction rather than by competition.

The consequence is that Pioneer status is a one-shot decision for both parties. An Agent must choose its single chain carefully because it can never hold the status again, and a chain must choose its Agent carefully because it cannot re-designate later. Both sides are pushed toward a durable commitment rather than an experiment.
description: Designation comes from the chain's own team or foundation and is verified by Operational GovOps against both constraints, making the status a scarce non-renewable asset on both sides.
